entry.evidence: The occurrence of saltwater intrusion in Agbabu is considered anomalous because the distance between Agbabu and the nearest saltwater intruded localities

sequences.source_document: Published paper PDF plus XML abstract and captions

steps.action: Take from earlier studies, including the first author's, that saltwater occurs in Agbabu about 30 km from the nearest saline localities, and call the occurrence anomalous.
steps.quote: The occurrence of saltwater intrusion in Agbabu is considered anomalous because the distance between Agbabu and the nearest saltwater intruded localities

steps.action: Pose the question of the origin or source of saltwater in Agbabu's inland aquifers.
steps.quote: The aim of this study is to determine the source of saltwater in the inland aquifers of Agbabu

steps.action: Following Allen et al. (2002), propose that a fracture network connecting Agbabu to the Atlantic Ocean conducts saltwater. Pumping and tidal activity are named as other influences. The hypothesis is restated on p. 15 as a major geological structure linking Agbabu to the saline zone or ocean.
steps.quote: There is a need to examine the fracture connectivity in Agbabu with the Atlantic Ocean, by employing magnetic method.

steps.action: Assign each method a role: aeromagnetics to test for a structural contribution, resistivity to map the layer sequence, saline zones and flow direction, and hydrochemistry to measure salinity indicators.
steps.quote: The aeromagnetic method was utilized to investigate the possibility of a structural contribution to the saline water origin.

steps.action: Collect the data: archival NGSA aeromagnetic survey data for the eastern Dahomey Basin; 13 Schlumberger VES (AB/2 = 225 m) plus 10 secondary VES from earlier work; two dipole-dipole ERT lines placed along suspected saline zones; and 11 water samples from wells, a borehole and the Oluwa River (pp. 8, 14-15).
steps.quote: Aeromagnetic data covering the eastern part of the Dahomey Basin was obtained from the Nigeria Geological Survey Agency (NGSA).

steps.action: Process the magnetic data (IGRF removal, RTE, upward continuation, analytic signal, total horizontal derivative, tilt derivative, Euler SI = 1, SPI). Read off three zones (A, B, C), two NE-SW fault zones forming a horst-graben pattern, and source depths of 542 m to 3.1 km (text pp. 15-19).
steps.quote: Therefore, zones A and C resembles horst structure while zone B is like a graben structure

steps.action: Check the fault-zone interpretation by comparing the SPI depth map with the other enhancement products of the same magnetic data.
steps.quote: The result from the SPI technique (Fig. 3f) exhibits correspondence with other data enhancement techniques in this study.

steps.action: Superimpose the SPI map on co-author Olayanju's (2015) map of inland deep-ocean fault zones (Fig. 4). Identify the mapped fault zones with the Chain Fracture Zone and decide to probe Agbabu with geoelectric and hydrochemical surveys.
steps.quote: the suspected fault zones that are revealed in this study coincide perfectly with the Chain Fracture Zone (CFZ) earlier delineated by Olayanju

steps.action: Interpret the VES curves by partial curve matching and WinResist inversion (rms ≤ 10) and invert the ERT lines. Build three geoelectric sections with four layers and flag low-resistivity (about 1-22 Ωm) zones in the bituminous sand as saline (Table 1, Fig. 6, pp. 15, 19-22).
steps.quote: The drastically low resistivity signatures (11 – 20 Ωm) that are prominent at 25 m depth

steps.action: Check the resistivity signature in two ways: a parametric sounding (VES 1) and ERT beside an abandoned saline borehole, confirmed as saline by residents; and a second ERT traverse that re-images the saline zone beneath VES 10 (pp. 19-20).
steps.quote: The suspected saline water intrusion zone beneath VES station 10 is further confirmed between 90 m and 160 m on the 2D ERT

steps.action: Compare the results with published work: resistivity ranges with saline-intrusion thresholds from Edet and Okereke (2001) and Ayolabi et al. (2013) (p. 20), and the fault zones with those from bitumen exploration by Amigun et al. (2012a).
steps.quote: The fault zones delineated in the geomagnetic section by Amigun et al. (2012a) and the aeromagnetic results correlate well with the fault zones

steps.action: Classify VES stations as saline or not saline at depth to build a salinity extent chart, and infer from it a direction of incursion from the east of the town (Fig. 7a-b).
steps.quote: It is possible that the incursion/intrusion of saline water into Agbabu might be coming from the eastern side of the town

steps.action: Compare the water-sample chemistry (chloride, conductivity, TDS) with WHO limits. Only S11, next to the abandoned borehole, exceeds them.
steps.quote: Laboratory analysis reveals that all but one of the water samples (S11) have chloride concentration below 74 mg /l.

steps.action: Explain the mostly fresh samples by an auxiliary assumption, that the samples come from shallower depths than the saline zones, rather than revising the resistivity interpretation.
steps.quote: the depth at which most of the delineated saline water zones exist is greater than the depth at which water samples were obtained

steps.action: Use ionic ratios (HCO3/Cl severity classes after Revelle, Todd and Fadili; SO4/Cl; Na/Cl) as an independent chemical check. S4 and S11 show Na-Cl facies, taken as confirming intrusion at the abandoned borehole (Table 4).
steps.quote: the water sample (S4 and S11) showcase Na-Cl water facies, which confirms the occurrence of saltwater intrusion into the freshwater aquifer at the abandoned borehole

steps.action: Report a sealed artesian saline-water well about 1 km northwest of the town centre (Plate 2) as further physical evidence.
steps.quote: Another physical manifestation of saline water in Agbabu is found about 1 km northwest of the town center

steps.action: Name a rival or contributing cause, over-abstraction and uncontrolled pumping of the few wells (repeated on p. 23). It is not tested.
steps.quote: Over-abstraction of the only available wells (Plates 1 and 2) by the teeming population in Agbabu deflates hydraulic conductivities of freshwater

steps.action: Combine the CFZ extension, the saline-zone distribution and the artesian well into a conceptual model of the saline source (Fig. 8).
steps.quote: A conceptual model of the origin or possible source of the saline water zones in Agbabu was developed from the findings of this study

steps.action: Take from oceanographic literature (Mercier and Morin 1997 and others) that the CFZ carries dense, saline bottom water. From this, expect pressurised bottom water to emerge as the artesian well.
steps.quote: The CFZ facilitates the transport of the Antarctic Bottom Water (ABW) and the Lower North Atlantic Deep Water (LNADW)

steps.action: Compare the patchy saline-zone pattern with Allen et al.'s (2002) expectation of localised intrusion in fractured aquifers connected to the ocean.
steps.quote: This assertion by Allen et al. (2002) best explains the localization of saltwater intruding fresh groundwater in some parts of Agbabu

steps.action: Keep transport of saline bottom water through the CFZ as the proposed main possible source, with pumping as a possible additional influence.
steps.quote: transport of saline bottom water from the ocean through the CFZ into the complex aquifers of Agbabu area is proposed

tree.answer: Inland saltwater at Agbabu, about 30 km from known saline localities, reported by earlier studies
No; the saline zones and fault zones are inferred from resistivity and magnetic data
Find the origin of the salinity
Fracture (CFZ) conduit from the ocean versus pumping or over-abstraction; named, not set against each other
No distinct predictions derived for the rivals
Conditions found: archival aeromagnetic data, and field VES, ERT and water samples
Partly: SPI agrees with the other filters, ERT re-images the VES 10 zone and VES 1 matches the saline borehole, but most water samples are fresh and this is explained by sampling depth
CFZ bottom-water transport proposed as the main possible source

end.claim: Saline bottom water transported from the Atlantic through the inland extension of the Chain Fracture Zone into Agbabu's aquifers is proposed as the main possible source of the anomalous saltwater.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the aeromagnetic inference of NE-SW fault zones crossing the basin to Agbabu, matched to the CFZ, there would be no link between the inland saline zones and the ocean.

gates.evidence: Action: the fracture-connectivity hypothesis (p. 3) motivated the aeromagnetic analysis, and the ERT lines were placed along suspected saline zones (p. 15). The aeromagnetic data were archival, and 10 VES came from earlier work. Claim: the saline-zone delineation faced checks that could fail (VES 1 beside the saline borehole, a second ERT line, hydrochemistry), and the hydrochemistry largely failed, which was protected by a sampling-depth auxiliary (p. 22). The source claim (CFZ bottom water) faced no test that could discriminate it from pumping or other sources. Registration: nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: WHO drinking-water guideline limits for chloride and TDS
R programming software for rescaling hydrochemical values into bubble charts

novelty_claims.quote: This study represents the first attempt to explain the origin of saline groundwater in Agbabu.
[...] include the discovery of the inland extension of the NW-SE trending Chain Fracture Zone

limits: The XML text supplied holds only the abstract and captions, so body quotes come from the PDF pages. No review file was supplied, so there is no review sequence. Process facts the paper does not show: (1) No test discriminates CFZ bottom-water transport from other saline sources (connate or bitumen-associated brines, pumping-induced upconing). No isotopes, Br/Cl or temperature data tie the water to Antarctic Bottom Water. That a fault zone carries pressurised ocean bottom water about 47 km inland is asserted from cited oceanography, not demonstrated. (2) The pumping rival is named but neither excluded nor tested. (3) Hydrochemistry mostly shows fresh water (10 of 11 samples), which is attributed to shallow sampling depth without data on well depths. The text also says other samples 'indicate the possible presence of saltwater intrusion', which conflicts with this. (4) Internal inconsistencies: CFZ trend given as both NE-SW and NW-SE. The CFZ extension is called a 'discovery' although the text says Olayanju (2015, a co-author) mapped it earlier. S11 TDS is given as 1005, 1004 and 1500 mg/l. The artesian well is cited as Plate 1 and as 'Fig. 11b', and 'Fig. 9' is cited, but neither figure exists. The eastern incursion direction sits beside an artesian saline well to the northwest. (5) Ten VES are secondary data from earlier work, the resistivity thresholds for saline zones are set by interpretation rather than stated in advance, and the data are not public. (6) Sub-claim statuses (inference): the saline-zone delineation is closest to estimate_with_resolution but gives no uncertainty; the CFZ inland extension is best_explanation, resting on correspondence with Olayanju (2015); the eastern incursion direction is best_explanation, weakly supported. (7) The composition is coded trace_series only loosely, since the rivals are not stated as competing explanations tested against the traces.

disagreements.target: Observatory wells and predictive flow models for assessing salinization (Werner et al. 2013; Goebel et al. 2019)
disagreements.support: Cites published limitations (point data, cost, calibration errors) to argue that geophysical methods are needed in addition; the paper offers no evidence of its own on this.
disagreements.quote: [...] and monitoring approaches fail to detect the subsurface complexity conditions because, they solely rely on discontinuous point data

alternatives_considered.reason: Good horizontal resolution, adequate depth of investigation, minimal inductive coupling, and good for vertical structures such as fractures and saline zones

alternatives_considered.chosen: Reduction to the equator and analytic signal
alternatives_considered.reason: Analytic signal is independent of field and magnetization direction and substitutes for RTP at low geomagnetic latitudes

alternatives_considered.chosen: Euler deconvolution with structural index SI = 1 (fault model)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Other structural indices (implied by the statement that a wrong index gives spurious depths)
alternatives_considered.reason: SI = 1 is typical of a fault model; a suitable index is said to be fundamental to unbiased depth estimation

alternatives_considered.chosen: Aeromagnetic analysis of the whole eastern Dahomey Basin rather than Agbabu alone
alternatives_considered.reason: Adeyemo et al. (2017) showed saline aquifers in the south, suggesting a structure linking Agbabu to the saline zone or ocean

alternatives_considered.chosen: Fracture connectivity (CFZ) as the main source
alternatives_considered.reason: Isolated, localised saline zones fit the expectation of Allen et al. (2002) for fractured aquifers
